title: Visit for polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
what: The doctor finds out why your cycle is irregular and checks your hormones and ovaries. Then they choose treatment based on your goals.
why: For rare or irregular periods, extra body hair, acne, or trouble getting pregnant.
duration: the visit usually takes 30 to 40 minutes; tests are usually ready in a few days
tell_doctor: What your cycle is like and when your last period was
If you want to get pregnant
If you or your relatives have diabetes
What medicines and hormones you take

prepare.title: Cycle diary
prepare.text: Write down your period dates for the last few months.

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Hormones are usually tested on certain days of the cycle. The doctor will tell you which days.

prepare.title: Documents
prepare.text: Bring past test results and ultrasounds.

steps: The doctor asks about your cycle and how you feel
Your height, weight, and blood pressure are measured
You get referrals for hormone and blood sugar tests
At the next visit, the doctor discusses the results and treatment
feel: A regular visit with nothing unpleasant
An internal ultrasound may be a little uncomfortable
after: Do the tests on the list
You are often advised to watch your diet and stay active
Treatment is chosen for your goal: a regular cycle or pregnancy
red_flags: Sudden pain low in your belly

faq.q: Can I get pregnant with PCOS?
faq.a: Yes, many women do, sometimes with the help of treatment.
PCOS usually does not go away completely, but the symptoms can be well controlled.

reminders.text: Gynecologist visit tomorrow. Bring your period dates and past test results.
